candidate.title: SPARE
candidate.scope: The SPARE middle row of the supplied Illumina poster crop: Specific Parallel Amplification of 5′ RNA Ends for identifying plant microRNA processing intermediates. The left hairpin and the word or introduce alternative biological base-to-loop and loop-to-base processing routes, not a laboratory split or two distinct assays. The upper route shows one intermediate/product form; the lower shows two, one retaining a red-marked segment. Each route independently proceeds through RNA-adapter ligation, reverse transcription with a precursor-specific primer, PCR yielding P5/P7-ended DNA and sequencing. Neighboring Structure-Seq/DMS-Seq above and PARS/dsRNA-Seq below are context, not targets or inputs. This is a schematic architecture; the supplied primary content is an abstract, not full text. Unshown rRNA depletion and size selection mentioned in the secondary catalogue are not expanded into graph operations. The secondary page also lists a Ma et al. plant-miRNA review and describes a Schmidt et al. human NMD application; neither primary source is available here and neither defines an additional target or supplies reaction evidence for this extraction.

operations.label: Base to loop processing
operations.description: Biological processing of the foldback precursor is depicted in the base-to-loop direction, yielding one illustrated intermediate form. These arrows explain the origin of the assayed RNA ends; they do not specify an added in vitro cleavage reaction.
operations.mechanism: The primary abstract reports DCL1 and accessory proteins recognizing precursor structure and cleaving at specific sites. No specific bond chemistry or release stoichiometry is supplied here.
operations.information_effect: The resulting RNA fragments carry processing-end positions. The illustrated routes differ in how many intermediate forms are represented; the drawing does not quantify their abundance or establish the mechanism of differential recovery.

Abstract: precursor cleavage machinery
evidence.quote: Still, the miRNA processing machinery, consisting of DICER-LIKE1 (DCL1) and accessory proteins recognize structural features on the precursors to cleave them at specific places releasing the mature miRNAs.

operations.label: RNA-adapter ligation
operations.description: Add an RNA adapter, drawn green, to the 5′ end of the uncapped processing intermediates in the base-to-loop route. Output differs by the appended terminal adapter while retaining the illustrated RNA forms.
operations.information_effect: Creates an adapter-to-RNA boundary that marks the captured RNA end. This selects an uncapped-end population; capture alone does not prove that every molecule arose from DCL1 cleavage.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title, middle-row SPARE caption and verified catalogue heading agree. Base-to-loop and loop-to-base are alternative biological processing directions within SPARE, each drawn with its own ligation, RT, PCR and sequencing route. The primer label belongs to RT, resolved by the primary abstract. Both routes are preserved as separate local operation instances; no merge or pooling operation is depicted. The paper association is resolved at abstract level for the plant-miRNA implementation, without importing the human NMD application or the neighboring methods.
